newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Fox says would accept PAN nomination.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Fox says would accept PAN nomination.

text.p: A leading figure in Mexico's conservative opposition National Action Party (PAN) said on Monday he would accept his party's nomination for president if it were offered to him for the 2000 elections.

Vicente Fox, the governor of central Guanajuato state, said during a trip to San Diego, California, that "I would accept the responsibility" of running as the PAN's presidential candidate, the state news agency Notimex said.
He also said he would use "all my efforts" to ensure that an opposition party wins in 2000, Notimex reported.
Fox, a charismatic politician known for wearing cowboy boots and shunning a necktie, is considered a frontrunner for the party's nomination.
Moreover the PAN is seen as having a decent chance of breaking the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party's (PRI's) 68-year hold on power in the next presidential vote.
But it was highly unusual for a Mexican politician to even speak about accepting a candidacy so far in advance.
The PAN as well as Mexico's centre-left opposition, the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), have made big gains against the PRI in local state elections in the past two years.
Many pollsters and analysts predict the PRI will lose in the first-ever election for governor of Mexico City on July 6. In the past, a regent, or mayor, of Mexico City was appointed by the president.
